The FOMC acknowledges that COVID-19 will depress near-term activity and raise downside risks, but—consistent with the credit-channel literature (e.g., Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Oliner and Rudebusch; Gertler and Gilchrist)—cutting rates to the lower bound alongside large-scale Treasury/MBS purchases, expanded repos, and dollar swap lines should ease money-market pressures, lower external finance premia, and support business investment and household spending. With inflation below target and longer-run expectations little changed (aligned with Svensson’s inflation-forecast-targeting insights), these actions stabilize financial conditions and reduce liquidity-trap amplification, even though monetary policy can only accommodate—not reverse—a largely supply-driven pandemic shock.
